version.changelog:
Version 4.0.0 introduces new advanced interview preparation features:

- Added 7-day sprint planning for intensive short-term preparation.
- Introduced job readiness scoring to assess and track interview preparedness.
- Enabled answer rewriting to help users improve and polish interview answers.
- Expanded trigger phrases to include "冲刺计划", "就绪度", "润色答案" for broader interaction scenarios.
- All previous features (difficulty levels, question types, interview history, radar charts, document and interactive modes) are retained.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ai-interview-coach
Version: 4.0.0

The ai-interview-coach skill bundle is a comprehensive interview preparation assistant. Its instructions (SKILL.md) guide an AI agent to analyze resumes, generate tailored questions, and conduct mock interviews. It includes features for local history tracking (storing data in ~/.ai-interview-coach/), progress analysis, and answer refinement. The logic is transparent and strictly aligned with its stated purpose, with no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (generate interview questions from a resume or role) matches its instructions and requirements; it requests no credentials or installs and is instruction-only.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the runtime instructions: the skill reads resumes or job-role input and generates difficulty-controlled interview questions, mock-interview flows, progress tracking and reports. All declared functionality (question generation, difficulty detection, different formats) is justified by the instructions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions explicitly direct the agent to read local resume files (MD/PDF/DOCX) and to extract text (mentions a 'PDF tool'). They also describe saving history and sessions under ~/.ai-interview-coach. This is consistent with a coaching skill, but it implies file I/O and use of a PDF extraction capability (unspecified). Confirm whether file parsing happens locally or is uploaded to an external service before use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or code files are included (instruction-only), so nothing is written to disk by an installer and no external packages are pulled in. This is the lowest-risk delivery model.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, binaries, or config paths. Requested access (reading user-provided resume files and optionally writing a local history directory described in README) is proportional to the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Flags are default (not always:true). README/SKILL.md describe saving history and session files in ~/.ai-interview-coach; that is reasonable for this skill but means it will persist user data locally if implemented. Because the skill is instruction-only, persistence depends on the host agent's implementation — verify where and how history is stored.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and does what it says: read a resume or role description, generate interview questions and (optionally) keep local practice history. Before installing or using it, consider: 1) Privacy of resume data — the skill expects you to provide file paths; only supply files you are comfortable the host agent can access, or redact sensitive PII. 2) PDF extraction method — confirm whether extraction runs locally or uploads files to an external service; avoid uploading sensitive documents to unknown endpoints. 3) Local history storage — README mentions ~/.ai-interview-coach; if you prefer not to persist records, check whether you can disable history saving. 4) Since this is instruction-only with no code files, the host agent determines actual behavior (file reads, any network calls). If you need stronger guarantees, ask the skill author or host for details on where parsing happens and how stored data is protected.
